summary:
Project Segrebot is an innovative, low-cost search and rescue system designed to help locate people trapped under debris during landslides and building collapses. The project aims to improve rescue operations by using electronic sensors and smart technology to identify possible human presence in disaster-affected areas.
The proposed system uses sensors to detect vibrations and other signals that may indicate the presence of survivors. It can process the collected information and communicate alerts and location-related information to rescue teams through wireless communication.
The main goal of Project Segrebot is to reduce the time required to locate trapped individuals, improve the efficiency of rescue operations, and support emergency response teams in dangerous environments. By developing a cost-effective and reliable solution, this project aims to contribute to disaster management and help save lives.
details:
Our project, Field Shift, aims to develop a smart agricultural decision-support system that helps farmers adapt to changing environmental and climatic conditions.

The system combines NASA Earth-observation data, including rainfall, temperature and soil moisture information, with local soil conditions and crop characteristics. It analyzes environmental factors that affect agricultural productivity and helps farmers explore suitable crop rotation strategies.

The proposed platform will provide an easy-to-understand interface where farmers can enter their farm location, soil details, crop information and agricultural priorities. Based on the available data, the system will help compare different crop rotation options.

The main objective is to promote sustainable agriculture, improve soil health, conserve water and help farmers prepare for changing climate conditions.

This project connects space technology with practical agricultural needs and aims to support farmers in making more informed farming decisions.
